check_box.name: volumetric_check
check_box.label: Draw the volumetric cloud field
check_box.tool_tip: Off leaves the sky to the dome alone - no puffs and no under deck, and so nothing for lightning to hide behind or for precipitation to fall out of

check_box.name: procedural_noise_check
check_box.label: Grow a noise map when the sky authors none
check_box.tool_tip: Holes, towers and the anvil carving still happen on a plain sky: the map is grown from the weather seed, so every client sharing the environment gets the same geography without anyone uploading a texture. Off leaves an unauthored deck evenly covered

check_box.name: tessellation_check
check_box.label: Tessellate puffs (anvil skirt)
check_box.tool_tip: Each puff becomes a 4x4 grid of sub-quads instead of one flat card, so the top rows can shear along the wind, curl down and dissolve - the anvil skirt, which no amount of fragment noise can fake on geometry that is not there. The skirt itself only appears on puffs the deck gave an anvil to, but the finer grid also samples the sky lighting and aerial perspective per sub-quad rather than per corner. Costs sixteen times the vertices

check_box.name: cloud_overlay_check
check_box.label: Draw the cloud field
check_box.tool_tip: The field's view, picked below. Same overlay as Develop > Render Metadata > Cloud Field

combo_box.name: C_cloud_view
combo_box.tool_tip: Cell gate and towers: the builder's 260m grid replayed across the field, green where cloud was placed and red where the sky was left open, with a stalk as tall as the noise map wants that column to climb. Column profiles: for nearby cells, the column that cell grows outlined at its true position and altitude, its width at each height exactly what the profile ramp and the anvil give a puff there - the curve as a shape, standing beside the cloud it made
